title: A unified approach to interpreting model predictions
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NIPS 2017), Long Beach, CA, USA. Curran Associates, Inc.
harvard_reference: Lundberg, S.M. and Lee, S.-I. (2017) 'A unified approach to interpreting model predictions', in Guyon, I. et al. (eds) Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NIPS 2017). Long Beach, CA, USA. Curran Associates, Inc., pp. 4765-4774. Available at: https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2017/hash/8a20a8621978632d76c43dfd28b67767-Abstract.html (Accessed: 27 September 2026).
abstract_summary: The paper argues that understanding why a model makes a prediction matters as much as accuracy, but the most accurate models (ensembles, deep networks) are hard to interpret, and the many post-hoc explanation methods proposed have unclear relationships. It introduces SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), a unified framework that assigns each feature an importance value for a particular prediction. Its two novel components are (1) identifying a new class of additive feature attribution methods and (2) theoretical results showing a unique solution in that class with desirable properties. The class unifies six existing methods (LIME, DeepLIFT, layer-wise relevance propagation, Shapley regression values, Shapley sampling values and Quantitative Input Influence), several of which lack those properties. Building on this, the authors propose new estimation methods (e.g. Kernel SHAP, Deep SHAP) with better computational performance and/or closer agreement with human intuition.

claims_supported.claim: SHAP values unify several additive feature-attribution methods under Shapley-value axioms (local accuracy, missingness, consistency) and provide per-prediction explanations.
claims_supported.where: Abstract: 'we present a unified framework for interpreting predictions, SHAP ... SHAP assigns each feature an importance value for a particular prediction ... The new class unifies six existing methods'. Section 2 (Additive Feature Attribution Methods) shows LIME, DeepLIFT, layer-wise relevance propagation, Shapley regression values, Shapley sampling values and Quantitative Input Influence all fit Definition 1. Section 3 (Simple Properties Uniquely Determine Additive Feature Attributions) states Property 1 (Local accuracy), Property 2 (Missingness) and Property 3 (Consistency), and Theorem 1 proves the Shapley-value formula (Eq. 8) is the only explanation model satisfying all three. Section 4 defines SHAP values as this unique solution. Note the paper calls these 'properties' (from cooperative game theory) rather than 'axioms'; the substance of the claim is accurate.

verification_notes: Crossref bibliographic search returned only unrelated works (NeurIPS proceedings are not Crossref-registered), so the work was verified directly at the official proceedings site (papers.nips.cc / proceedings.neurips.cc abstract page and bibtex), via Semantic Scholar (arXiv:1705.07874; CorpusId 21889700; venue Neural Information Processing Systems; pages 4765-4774) and via OpenAlex. The official NeurIPS PDF was downloaded and its text extracted: the running header reads '31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017), Long Beach, CA, USA'; embedded metadata gives Book = 'Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30', firstpage 4765, lastpage 4774, Publisher = Curran Associates, Inc., Editors = I. Guyon, U.V. Luxburg, S. Bengio, H. Wallach, R. Fergus, S. Vishwanathan, R. Garnett, EventType = Oral. The official bibtex lists volume 30, the same editors and publisher, but leaves the pages field empty; the page range 4765-4774 comes from the PDF metadata and Semantic Scholar. Section 2, Section 3 (Properties 1-3, Theorem 1) and the abstract sentence on per-prediction importance were confirmed verbatim in the extracted text and independently in the ar5iv rendering of the arXiv version. DOI field left empty because the proceedings paper has no registered DOI; the arXiv preprint carries the arXiv-assigned DOI 10.48550/arXiv.1705.07874 (OpenAlex), which identifies the preprint rather than the NeurIPS version. Issue field is not applicable. Conference dates and publisher place were not verified in this session and are therefore omitted from the reference.
caveats: No DOI exists for the NeurIPS proceedings version; if the report's reference list requires a DOI, cite the arXiv preprint separately as Lundberg, S.M. and Lee, S.-I. (2017) 'A unified approach to interpreting model predictions', arXiv. doi:10.48550/arXiv.1705.07874 - but be aware the arXiv text lacks the NeurIPS header and pagination. The paper itself uses the term 'properties' rather than 'axioms' for local accuracy, missingness and consistency. The lead's 'NeurIPS 30' is fine in substance, but the 2017 conference was branded 'NIPS 2017' at the time; the proceedings series is 'Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30'.
